truncation_risk_near_num_predict_ceiling.verdict: Zero captions in this dump approach either ceiling (max observed ~142 tokens vs a 400-token first-attempt budget). No truncation-risk signal in this population.

outlier_example.note: qid 3 and qid 8 got byte-identical captions; qid 7 got a differently-worded (same-content) caption for the exact same frame. Single outlier out of 535 -- 99.8% cache-consistency, not a systemic issue. Most likely a re-caption on a cache miss/race rather than the per-video cache itself misbehaving.

cache_reuse_across_qids.verdict: The per-video caption cache is behaving as designed: 534/535 (99.8%) of frames revisited by a later question in the same video reused the exact same caption text rather than re-captioning. Re-captioning per-question (for question-aware captions) would cost re-running the captioner on all 1665 distinct (video, frame_idx) pairs currently captioned once each -- i.e. up to 2556 calls if every question needed its own caption, roughly 1.5x today's 1665 real captioning calls.

qualitative_sample_seed_42_n_10: Nearly all sampled captions are generic itemized scene descriptions (objects/people/setting), NOT question-aware -- consistent with the captioner running question-blind (per the module docstring in scripts/blind_ablation_eval.py: 'question-blind captioning -- exactly reproduces the recorded run'). None of the 10 sampled captions reference the multiple-choice options or the specific temporal relation asked about; they read as what a generic dense-caption model would produce for any viewer, not what's relevant to a specific gold answer.

This is a known, deliberate property of this run's captioning path (focus_hint is optional and appears not to have been active in this dump), not a bug in the caption model itself -- but it is directly relevant to why Acc@GQA's gap decomposition (see tuning/family2-tuning-state memory) finds P(correct | grounded)=61.1% vs P(correct | NOT grounded)=51.7%: generic captions likely under-deliver the specific visual detail a temporal/causal question needs even when the retrieval span IS correct.
